description: SASRec predicts the next interaction using causal self-attention over a user's item history. Item and positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items through shared item embeddings. Training uses next-item positives and sampled negatives. Its central idea is to select relevant past actions adaptively, supporting both recent context and longer dependencies. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781)
motivation: The paper seeks to combine the simplicity of Markov models on sparse data with the longer-range modeling capacity of recurrent networks. For this task, SASRec supplies the starting baseline; the supplied description does not specify a new cold-start mechanism. Learned item embeddings alone provide limited support for items without training interactions.

Keep artifacts beneath the trial directory and synchronize the predictor writer with any architecture changes. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and the compatibility interface. No experiments or performance improvements are established by this summary.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the prescribed training split.
  Build left-padded, truncated histories and shifted next-item targets.
  Embed item IDs and positions.
  Apply causal attention and feed-forward blocks, masking padding.
  Score positive and sampled negative items; optimize binary cross-entropy.
  Save model weights, configuration, and matching predictor code.
Evaluate through the pinned validation protocol and compare macro HR@10.
